questions.question: Prepare a short note on PRSI
questions.solution_html:
• PRSI
  • • Public Relations Society of India, founded in 1958, is the apex body representing PR professionals in India
  • • It promotes ethical standards, professional development, and recognition of PR as a strategic discipline
  • • Organises national conventions, awards, and training programmes for PR practitioners across India
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: • Organises national conventions, awards, and training programmes for PR practitioners across India

questions.question: Analyse the need of two-way communication in governmental PR with suiatble examples
questions.solution_html:
• Two-way Communication in Governmental PR
  • • Two-way communication enables governments to both disseminate information and receive public feedback,
  • ensuring responsive governance
  • • Examples include public consultations on policy, grievance redressal portals, and town hall meetings
  • • It builds public trust, reduces misinformation, and ensures that government decisions reflect citizen needs
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: • It builds public trust, reduces misinformation, and ensures that government decisions reflect citizen needs

questions.question: Discuss the crisis communication function of Corporate Communication
questions.solution_html:
• Crisis Communication in Corporate Communication
  • • Crisis communication involves managing information flow during emergencies to protect organisational
  • reputation and maintain stakeholder trust
  • • It includes preparing crisis communication plans, designating spokespersons, and ensuring timely,
  • transparent messaging
  • • Effective crisis communication minimises reputational damage and demonstrates organisational
  • accountability and responsibility
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: accountability and responsibility

questions.question: Cite and explain the important points to be noted while preparing publicity messages
questions.solution_html:
• Points for Preparing Publicity Messages
  • • Messages must be accurate, newsworthy, timely, and tailored to the target audience and chosen media
  • platform
  • • Language should be clear, concise, and free of jargon, with a strong lead that captures attention immediately
  • • Messages should align with organisational objectives and maintain consistency with the overall brand
  • identity and tone
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: identity and tone

questions.question: Discuss the pillars on which CSR operates
questions.solution_html:
• Pillars of CSR
  • • CSR operates on the pillars of economic responsibility (profitability), legal responsibility (compliance), ethical
  • responsibility (fair conduct), and philanthropic responsibility (community contribution)
  • • It is guided by the principle that organisations have obligations beyond profit-making towards society and the
  • environment
  • • Stakeholder engagement, transparency, and sustainability are central to effective CSR practice
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: • Stakeholder engagement, transparency, and sustainability are central to effective CSR practice

questions.question: Discuss the importance of house journals in corporate communication
questions.solution_html:
• Importance of House Journals
  • • House journals serve as internal communication tools that keep employees informed, motivated, and aligned
  • with organisational goals and values
  • • They strengthen organisational culture, foster a sense of belonging, and recognise employee achievements
  • • Externally directed house journals also enhance corporate image and maintain relationships with clients,
  • partners, and stakeholders
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: partners, and stakeholders

questions.question: Describe the characteristics of an effective PR message
questions.solution_html:
• Characteristics of an Effective PR Message
  • • Must be clear, credible, consistent, and tailored to the specific audience and communication channel
  • • Should be timely, factually accurate, and aligned with the organisation's overall communication strategy
  • • An effective PR message evokes the desired response — whether awareness, attitude change, or action —
  • without being overtly promotional
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: without being overtly promotional

questions.question: Explain the role of account management department in a PR agency
questions.solution_html:
• Role of Account Management in a PR Agency
  • • The account management department serves as the primary liaison between the PR agency and its clients,
  • managing relationships and ensuring client satisfaction
  • • It coordinates the work of creative, media, and research teams to deliver campaigns aligned with client
  • objectives
  • • Account managers handle project timelines, budgets, reporting, and strategic counsel to clients
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: • Account managers handle project timelines, budgets, reporting, and strategic counsel to clients

questions.question: Define 'branding' in the context of PR and Corporate Communication
questions.solution_html:
• Branding in PR and Corporate Communication
  • • Branding in PR refers to the strategic process of creating and maintaining a distinct, positive identity and
  • reputation for an organisation in the minds of its publics
  • • It encompasses visual identity (logo, colours), verbal identity (tone, messaging), and behavioural identity
  • (values, conduct)
  • • Consistent branding across all communication channels builds trust, recognition, and long-term stakeholder
  • loyalty
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: loyalty

questions.question: Distinguish between in-house PR department and external PR agency
questions.solution_html:
• In-house PR Department vs. External PR Agency
  • • An in-house PR department consists of employees within the organisation who have deep institutional
  • knowledge but may lack objectivity and diverse expertise
  • • An external PR agency is an independent firm hired on a contractual basis, offering fresh perspectives,
  • specialised skills, and broader industry experience
  • • Organisations often use both in combination — in-house teams managing day-to-day communication while
  • agencies handle campaigns and crisis situations
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: agencies handle campaigns and crisis situations

questions.question: Explain how the lack of objectivity affects the functioning of an in-house PR team
questions.solution_html:
• Lack of Objectivity in In-house PR Teams
  • • In-house PR professionals may develop organisational loyalty that compromises their ability to critically
  • assess and communicate difficult or negative information
  • • This lack of objectivity can lead to biased messaging, delayed crisis response, and reluctance to advise
  • against management decisions
  • • It undermines credibility with media and external publics who may perceive in-house communication as self-
  • serving
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: serving

questions.question: Explain the role of emotional intelligence in effective public relations management.
questions.solution_html:
• Emotional Intelligence in PR Management
  • • Emotional intelligence (EI) enables PR professionals to understand and manage their own emotions while
  • empathising with stakeholders, clients, and media representatives
  • • High EI improves conflict resolution, crisis communication, and relationship-building with diverse publics
  • • PR managers with strong EI are better equipped to craft empathetic messaging, navigate sensitive situations,
  • and maintain composure under pressure
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: and maintain composure under pressure

questions.question: PR is totally different frompublicity stunt.' Elaborate.
questions.solution_html:
• PR vs. Publicity Stunt
  • • PR is a planned, sustained, and strategic process aimed at building long-term mutual understanding between
  • an organisation and its publics
  • • Publicity stunts are short-term, attention-grabbing tactics that may generate media coverage but lack
  • strategic depth or relationship-building intent
  • • PR is grounded in ethics, credibility, and two-way communication; publicity stunts risk damaging reputation if
  • perceived as manipulative or insincere
  • • PR encompasses diverse functions — media relations, community engagement, crisis communication, CSR —
  • while a publicity stunt is a single tactical event
  • • Long-term organisational reputation is built through consistent PR practice, not isolated stunts that may
  • attract momentary attention without lasting goodwill
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: attract momentary attention without lasting goodwill

questions.question: Discuss in detail the roles and funtions of Corporate Communication.
questions.solution_html:
• Roles and Functions of Corporate Communication
  • • Managing corporate identity and ensuring consistent visual and verbal brand representation across all
  • internal and external communication
  • • Reputation management — proactively shaping public perception and responding to threats through media
  • relations and stakeholder engagement
  • • Internal communication — keeping employees informed, motivated, and aligned through newsletters,
  • intranets, and town halls
  • • Crisis communication — developing preparedness plans and managing organisational messaging during
  • emergencies to protect reputation
  • • Investor relations, CSR communication, and government/public affairs — maintaining trust and transparency
  • with all key stakeholder groups
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: with all key stakeholder groups

questions.question: Describe in detail the step-by-step process of designing and implementing a PR campaign, from fact-finding to evaluation.
questions.solution_html:
• Step-by-step Process of Designing a PR Campaign
  • • Fact-finding/Research — conducting situational analysis, audience research, and SWOT analysis to
  • understand the communication environment
  • • Goal-setting and Objectives — defining SMART objectives aligned with organisational communication goals
  • • Strategy and Planning — identifying target publics, key messages, communication channels, timelines, and
  • budget
  • • Implementation/Execution — deploying tactics such as press releases, events, social media campaigns, and
  • community outreach
  • • Evaluation — measuring outcomes against objectives using media monitoring, surveys, reach analytics, and
  • stakeholder feedback to assess campaign effectiveness
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: stakeholder feedback to assess campaign effectiveness

questions.question: Explain the purpose of campaigns in public relations. How do different campaign types serve different organizational objectives?
questions.solution_html:
• Purpose of PR Campaigns and Types
  • • PR campaigns are organised, purposeful communication efforts designed to achieve specific objectives —
  • building awareness, changing attitudes, managing crises, or promoting causes
  • • Awareness campaigns introduce new products, services, or issues to the public and generate media coverage
  • • Reputation/Image campaigns are used to rebuild or enhance public trust, particularly following negative
  • publicity or crises
  • • Advocacy campaigns seek to influence public policy, legislation, or social attitudes on behalf of the
  • organisation or a cause
  • • Internal campaigns target employees to build morale, communicate change, or reinforce organisational
  • values and culture
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: values and culture
